# PRESEPTAL CELLULITIS

Preseptal cellulitis involves soft tissues in front of the orbital septum and the eyelids and is often preceded by sinusitis. Infection does not involve the orbital contents. The most common pathogenic organisms in adults are streptococci, Haemophilus influenzae, anaerobes, and Staphylococcus aureus. Treat under the guidance of ophthalmology and/or otolaryngology. Intravenous antimicrobials are indicated initially for treatment of moderate to severe disease. Switch to oral antimicrobials when the patient's symptoms improve and the patient can tolerate oral medications.

---

References:

- Carlisle et al., American Family Physician. 2015, 92(2)106-112
- Mandell chapter: Periocular infections
- Johns Hopkins website
- Up-to-date article: Preseptal cellulitis
Therapy:
## Inpatient

### Treatment of mild to moderate disease

Preferred:
<AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) [R]

Alternative:
[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](beta-lactam-allergy-assessment)
Cefdinir 300 mg PO q12h ($) [R] <AND> trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 1 DS PO BID ($) [R,DI] for 5 days
Treatment of severe disease

Preferred:
Ampicillin-sulbactam 3 gm IV q6h ($) [R] <AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($)
[R] for 5 days

Alternative:
[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](beta-lactam-allergy-assessment)
Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h ($) [M] <AND> metronidazole 1000 mg IV q12h ($) [DI]
<AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) [R] for 5 days

*Local guidance (St. Cloud CDSS, Inpatient):*
Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg PO BID ($) [R] < AND> Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 1 DS PO BID ($) [R,DI] for 5 days

## Outpatient

### Treatment of mild to moderate disease

Preferred:
Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 1 DS PO BID ($) [R,DI] for 5 days

Alternative:
Cefdinir 300 mg PO q12h ($) [R] <AND> trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 1 DS PO
